name: field keys follow-up: shelf listing, JU-06A instruments, pad rename

pr.title: Follow up on field keys: list the instruments on a miss, add juno and bass, and rename still-water-pad to pad
pr.head: 8447be4e61ba3834e4f708224b4c894873167c7d

summary: field keys turns the computer keyboard into a MIDI source. Given an instrument name, it also plays a SuperCollider program live. A bare name such as pad resolves to shared/instruments/pad.scd, the project's instruments shelf, by the same rule a supercollider: track entry uses. This pull request collects the fixes from the first hands-on testing after the keyboard-instrument work merged in #178 to #182.

• A missing name lists the shelf. Before, field keys bass printed only that the file did not exist. Now the error lists every program on the shelf, split into those that play from notes and those that only render.
  • Two more playable instruments. examples/bloom gains juno and bass, ports of the JU-06A synth from the okamnesiac/offset repository.
  • still-water-pad becomes pad. The example's sine pad gets a shorter name in the example, the docs, and the plan.
  • A longer budget for a flaky test. The keymap reload test gets 20 s instead of vitest's default 5 s.

The review at this head found one blocking problem: the listing prints a program named pad.v2.scd as pad.v2, a name field keys cannot resolve. It also found that the reload test still fails under load, because the first file event is sometimes lost rather than late, and a longer budget cannot bring a lost event back. Both are flagged at their lines below.

cards.title: Terms this page uses
cards.html:
• Shelf: shared/instruments/, where a bare instrument name resolves.
  • Bare name: a name with no /. instrumentProgram adds .scd to it only when it has no extension at all.
  • Voice mode: a program run with FIELD_MODE=voice. Its value must be a SynthDef that the voice host plays once per note.
  • Render mode: the same program run by a build, writing a WAV file offline.
  • Voice host: the sclang process running sc/voice-host.scd, which plays an instrument live.
  • JU-06A: a SuperCollider model of the Roland Juno's signal chain, from okamnesiac/offset.

cards.title: Review at this head
cards.html:

  • pnpm typecheck passes. The two key test files pass 25 of 25 in sequential runs, and the reload test failed 3 of 8 concurrent runs.

groups.title: A missing instrument name lists the shelf
groups.kicker: The error from resolveInstrument now names every program on the shelf, split by whether it plays from notes
intro: When you name an instrument that is not on the shelf, resolveInstrument still throws, and the CLI still prints the message and exits 1. The message now ends with the shelf's contents. shelfInstruments reads shared/instruments/, keeps regular files whose names end in .scd, and sorts them. It puts a program under plays from notes when its text contains FIELD_MODE, and under renders only otherwise.

The text test is a shortcut that holds because voice is the only value FIELD_MODE takes. A program that never mentions the variable cannot answer voice mode, so reading the text is enough, and the error does not start sclang once per program.
Outside a project, a bare name still fails before any listing, because there is no shelf to list. Inside a project, a path that does not exist lists the shelf too.

checks.text: The shelf is shared/instruments/. A bare name has no /, and instrumentProgram adds .scd to it only when it has no extension at all. That rule is what the open thread turns on.

files.note: resolveInstrument appends the listing. shelfInstruments builds it, and describeShelf formats it.

checks.text: The open review thread (P2). This line strips .scd from every file name, but instrumentProgram adds it back only to a name with no extension. So a shelf program pad.v2.scd lists as pad.v2, and field keys pad.v2 then fails and prints the same list. Keep .scd when the stripped name still has an extension.
entry.isFile() is false for a directory named *.scd and for the dangling .#name.scd link Emacs leaves while a buffer is unsaved, so the listing never tries to read either.
see docs/keys.md is a path in Field's checkout, but the message prints in the user's project, which has no such file. The review suggests naming Field's doc and its section instead.
Ran field keys organ in examples/bloom at this head with no terminal attached. It exits 1 and prints exactly the listing docs/keys.md shows, before any terminal, MIDI, or sclang work starts.

files.note: A new case lists an empty shelf, then a shelf with one playable program, one render-only program, a text file, and a directory named folder.scd. The instrumentPath cases follow the rename to pad.

checks.text: Ran pnpm exec vitest run src/keys/voice-host.test.ts src/keys/keymap.test.ts at this head three times. Every case in this file passed each time.

groups.title: Two JU-06A instruments in examples/bloom
groups.kicker: juno and bass port offset's Juno model, and each both plays from notes and renders
intro: Before this change, the sine pad was the only example instrument you could play from the keyboard. juno.scd and bass.scd port the JU-06A from the okamnesiac/offset repository. It models the Roland Juno's chain: oscillators (saw, pulse, sub, and noise), a high-pass filter, a resonant low-pass filter, and an amplifier under one ADSR envelope, then a chorus.

Each program answers both modes. In voice mode, its last expression is a SynthDef with the freq, amp, gate, and out controls the voice host sets. The SynthDef writes two channels and frees itself when its envelope ends. In render mode, the program renders a short demo offline: juno holds a C minor ninth chord, and bass plays offset's eight-note line.

The two files repeat the same ju06a function on purpose. A program's own bytes are the cache key for what it renders. A shared file loaded at run time could change the sound without invalidating the renders that used it.

checks.text: This review did not start sclang, so nothing here was rendered or played. The pull request body reports that both renders peak below 0 dBFS and repeat byte for byte with a fixed seed.

files.note: The classic Juno pad: saw and pulse with the pulse width swept, a slow attack, a long release, and the chorus on.

checks.text: Compared every knob with the "Classic Juno pad" in offset's sessions/juno.scd, and the ju06a graph with offset's patches/ju06a.scd, by reading both. They match.
The chord's note-offs are added between its note-ons, out of time order. Score sorts its events when it is built, so the order does not matter.

files.note: offset's bass: one saw, a square sub an octave down, a filter the envelope opens on each note, and no chorus. It plays at true pitch.

checks.text: Compared every knob with the ~ju06a factory defaults in offset's patches/ju06a.scd, by reading both. They match.

groups.title: still-water-pad becomes pad
groups.kicker: The example's sine pad gets a shorter name everywhere except the plan's records of past runs
intro: shared/instruments/still-water-pad.scd moves to pad.scd, and its two SynthDefs become padKey and padVoice. The creek track pad-sc now names source: pad.scd, and the docs, the example's README, the repository README, and the keyboard-instrument plan use the new name.
The plan's verification tables in §10.3 and §13.3 keep the old name, because those rows record runs made under it. A new note in §13.2 says so.
A render's cache key includes the program's bytes, and the rename changes them, so pad-sc renders once more on its next build.

checks.text: git grep still-water-pad at this head finds only the plan's §10.3 and §13.3 rows and the note about them. field check in examples/bloom, the step CI runs, prints ok.

files.note: Renamed from still-water-pad.scd. Only the header comment and the two SynthDef names change.
The render entry names the renamed program.
The plan is in-progress, so its design text and acceptance criteria follow the current name. §13.2 gains the note about the rows that keep the old one.

groups.title: A longer budget for the keymap reload test
groups.kicker: The test gets 20 s, but its failure under load is a lost file event, not a slow one
intro: watchKeymap reloads a keymap file when you save it, by watching the file's directory. Its test saves three times and waits up to 5 s for each reload, all inside vitest's default 5 s budget for the whole test. The test timed out twice in full-suite runs, and this change raises its budget to 20 s.

Under load at this head the test still fails, with no reload 1 within 5 s. That message comes from the per-reload deadline, not from the test's budget. The first save's event is sometimes lost: the test saves right after it starts the watch, and the macOS directory watch is not yet live. Re-saving the first edit until its reload arrives recovered every lost event in the review's runs. The same race exists before this change.

files.note: Only the test's budget changes, with a comment giving the reason.

checks.text: From the review's suggestions: in eight concurrent runs at this head, three failed with no reload 1 within 5 s. In 60 timed runs under load, 4 first reloads never arrived within 30 s, and the rest arrived within 85 ms, so the runs showed no event "a second or more late". Re-save the first edit every 500 ms until reload 1 arrives.

intro: docs/keys.md is the user guide for field keys. Under "Play an instrument" it now shows the listing that a missing name prints, and it lists the three instruments in examples/bloom that answer voice mode. Its examples use the new name pad.

checks.text: The listing block matches what field keys organ prints at this head, apart from the path's prefix.
